title: UnitedHealth UNH Stock Slides 20% as Breakup Pressure and Medicare Audit Threats Hit the Healthcare Insurers - FXLeaders
content: UnitedHealth UNH stock plunged below $330 as proposed Medicare audit reforms, political calls to break up healthcare conglomerates and rising medical costs threaten insurers’ earnings and margins. Healthcare stocks extended their decline on Wednesday after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed tougher oversight of Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and the health insurance marketplace. UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) has been among the hardest hit, falling approximately 20% in three sessions and slipping below $330. Proposed Medicare Advantage audit reforms, political pressure to break up large healthcare conglomerates and rising medical costs are combining to undermine investor confidence in the sector. A major catalyst emerged on November 16, when CMS proposed the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare, or CRUSH rule. The proposal would formalise risk-adjustment data validation audits and allow regulators to extrapolate findings from sampled claims across entire Medicare Advantage contracts. Audits could extend back to payment year 2018, with CMS estimating that the framework could recover approximately $9 billion annually across the industry. UnitedHealth faces considerable exposure because it operates the country’s largest Medicare Advantage business. Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes identified UnitedHealth and Humana as the insurers most vulnerable to the proposed changes, followed by CVS Health, Elevance Health, Centene and Molina Healthcare. Political pressure is creating another headwind. Senator Elizabeth Warren has called for breaking up vertically integrated healthcare conglomerates, specifically naming UnitedHealth, CVS and Cigna while supporting the proposed Break Up Big Medicine Act. Restrictions on insurers owning pharmacy benefit managers and healthcare providers could threaten UnitedHealth’s integrated Optum business model. Such measures could limit operational flexibility, increase compliance costs and potentially weaken the advantages of its vertically integrated structure. UnitedHealth shares have come under renewed selling pressure, falling approximately 9% on Wednesday after failing to consolidate gains above $400. The stock has retreated into the $320s, with investors reassessing the regulatory and operational risks facing the managed-care sector. Insurers are also facing elevated medical utilisation, particularly across outpatient and specialty services. If healthcare costs continue rising faster than premiums, underwriting profitability could deteriorate, adding pressure to earnings forecasts. UnitedHealth retains significant scale and cash-flow generation, but the combination of regulatory uncertainty, potential Medicare payment recoveries and higher medical costs leaves its shares vulnerable. Investors will be watching management guidance and the $350 area as an important technical reference, while a sustained recovery will likely require greater clarity on the potential financial impact of the CMS proposal.

That segment, which spans pharmacy services, care delivery and analytics, has become central to how the company frames its path forward, and management described it as a steadier engine that can help smooth the swings felt on the benefits side during a period of elevated medical trends. title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Climb Ahead Of Anthropic’s Record Debut: SLS, GLD, TTWO, UNH In Focus - Stocktwits
content: U.S. stock futures traded higher overnight late Wednesday as markets geared up for Anthropic’s public trading. As of 10:49 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 0.41%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.63% and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed more than 1%. On Wednesday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed more than 650 points to end the session 1.11% lower, while the S&P 500 fell 0.23%. The Nasdaq Composite closed in the green, ending the session 0.42% higher. This week, all eyes have been on Anthropic’s debut on stock markets, which begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.” The AI company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, as per a post from the company. It also upsized its offering, selling approximately 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s (SPCX) record IPO. Ross Gerber, Co-Founder, CEO and CIO at Gerber Kawasaki, congratulated the company on its upcoming debut, saying in a post on X, “Incredible. Congrats Anthropic.  Let the AI era truly begin. $ANT.” Pro Capital (BRR) CEO Anthony Pompliano said in a post on X, “The Anthropic IPO is going to remind everyone how insane markets can be sometimes.” The AI trade has been struggling in recent weeks amid a technology rout and a fallout in Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) dominance following CEO Jensen Huang’s infidelity reports and subsequent resignation. “It’ll be an important barometer for investors’ AI appetite,” Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said to CNBC about the IPO. “AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations,” Cox added. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve’s minutes released on Wednesday weighed on market sentiment as policymakers flagged inflation concerns and AI risks. The central bank’s policymakers called artificial intelligence “a material source of inflation risk” in their latest minutes from the October meeting, adding that “off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint.” Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in the December meeting as inflationary concerns continue to mount. A day earlier, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon. Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly also noted that further interest rate hikes will be needed to ensure inflation returns to the central bank's 2% target. However, Daly suggested adopting a more “measured pace” to evaluate shifting economic conditions. The comments sparked a selloff in markets and weighed on precious metals, sending gold and silver prices to their lowest levels in more than a year. As per Bitcoin Archive, gold and silver’s 10% drop over the last nine days have wiped out $3.3 trillion in market value, larger than Nvidia’s over $1 trillion loss since Huang’s exit. Meanwhile, markets will be watching out for weekly jobless claims on Thursday, and earnings from Walmart Inc. (WMT) and clothing retailer Gap Inc. (GAP). SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc. (SLS): The company’s shares plunged nearly 13% in the overnight session, paring phenomenal gains from Tuesday when the company revealed positive topline results for Phase 3 Regal trial of its cancer vaccine galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after it announced a discounted public offering worth $150 million. SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD): The gold-linked exchange-traded fund was on the retail radar amid a steep decline in the price of the yellow metal amid a rising dollar and Fed’s hawkish comments. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (TTWO): The gaming company’s shares surged at close and continued to climb overnight after its Grand Theft Auto VI game garnered overwhelmingly positive early reviews and its Metacritic score came in at 99 out of 100. UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH): Shares of the company fell over 10% after Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed tighter Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud audits and oversight, potentially increasing compliance and documentation requirements for managed care providers such as UnitedHealth. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher in the overnight session. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 5.056%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.398%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.19% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday, with South Korea's KOSPI and China’s SSE Composite trading lower at the time of writing, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 was in the green. As Anthropic prepares to go public, “The Big Short” investor Michael Burry sees a rally he might eventually short and also detailed in Nvidia’s earnings he couldn’t overlook: the chipmaker was waiting longer to get paid. “It is pumping futures for now,” Burry said in his Substack chat when a reader asked about the IPO. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 apiece, above its proposed $70 to $78 range, ahead of Thursday’s expected Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. Burry had already said he would pass on the offering and on buying shares afterward. He put Anthropic’s commitments at more than $1 trillion and questioned whether revenue could grow fast enough to cover them. When asked whether to buy AI stocks through year-end or sell into a rebound, Burry said he was willing to wait for a better entry on the bearish side. “I cannot give advice but I will look to short on any rip, though I may let it run for a bit; the average bear market rally in both the 1930s and the 2000s was 22%,” he said. He had made a similar trade last week, doubling his Nasdaq-100 put position when the index bounced from around 27,000. He also bought back some puts on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) after trimming the bet. Burry went into Nvidia’s (NVDA) earnings holding $140 puts expiring in February 2027 and passed on buying short-dated calls to cushion the bet. After the results, he said he planned to spend less time covering Nvidia, but one number stood out. Days sales outstanding, a measure of how long it takes to collect payment, rose to 64 days from 60. Customers owed Nvidia $81 billion at quarter-end, as quarterly revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to $115.8 billion. “Without Jensen there I wonder how this improves - customers will find it harder to pay, or will just take more time to pay, I imagine,” Burry said, referring to former CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia attributed the increase to the timing of Rubin chip shipments and longer payment terms for some investment-grade customers. Burry also flagged the wait for Nvidia’s 10-Q, which interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said would arrive in the coming weeks. When a reader questioned why the earnings call lasted just 48 minutes including Q&A, Burry replied, “Earnings calls are controlled environments, and with over 70 sell side analysts covering it, clearly this was invitation only with some instruction.” When asked how much weight to give the SEC investigation into Nvidia, Burry said, “The SEC just doesn't have the resources or ability to do much.” A reader who identified themselves as a law firm owner challenged Burry to give an AI agent five years of company filings and ask it to flag changes in depreciation assumptions, down to the exact footnotes. “As a business owner, I know what an afternoon of my team’s time is worth. Give me that afternoon back every week and I’ll gladly write that check every month,” the reader said. Burry agreed that kind of tool was coming. He said that businesses could run smaller models on their own machines, using their own records. He said rising costs in China showed how expensive inference (the work a model does to answer a question) could become in the U.S. He also pointed to compression as a way to fit models onto smaller devices. “I know of people creating their own SLMs inside their homes with AI servers in house. This works against the Anthropic model and the Nvidia model. Brute force and mass resource usage is not the way forward,” he said, referring to small language models. Nvidia already makes hardware for the market. Its Nemotron 3.5 Bolt model can run on GeForce RTX graphics cards. Meanwhile, Tencent accounted for just over 2% of Burry’s portfolio earlier this month. The company subsequently reported negative quarterly free cash flow of 69.1 billion yuan. “It is concerning and the main reason I have not added. I am not sure, if AI bulls are correct, when the hyperscaler spending actually stops or is reduced,” Burry said, referring to spending by the biggest cloud computing companies. He also questioned whether bargain hunters in private credit were moving too soon. “I've heard capital is already being mobilized to pick at depressed private credit. Could be a self-fulfilling prophecy, but if the size of the AI boom's bust is large enough at the data center level, moves today would likely be overwhelmed and proven early,” he said. Burry also explained why his buy target for Netflix (NFLX) had fallen to the high $30s. In July, he had put the low $50s just outside his buying range and questioned the staying power of its hits. “Disney produces wine. Netflix produces milk,” he said at the time. In the latest chat, Burry said streaming rivals had caught up. “The process of producing hit shows has been a fraught exercise for a long time, and reality TV is a sign of rot in that creative process. It is the cheap more certain option, but one that does not breed network loyalty,” he said. Burry was equally open about Ero Copper (ERO). In September, he saw a mismatch that favored the miner. Data centers could lift copper demand within two or three years, while new deposits could take about 18 years to reach production. “My investment in ERO was ill-timed. I still own it in small size but have not added but once,” he said in the latest chat. “I will continue to evaluate it but I think this one has more to it than the AI trade. As I said it is not often I get bullish on a miner.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (NVDA) could remain an artificial intelligence powerhouse even without Jensen Huang, according to tech analyst Dan Ives, who sees the chipmaker as critical to U.S. economic future. He added that Nvidia’s AI dominance was bigger than one executive and its chip technology was two to three years ahead of its competitors. Calling Nvidia the “central nervous system” of the U.S. economy, Ives highlighted its central role in AI and capital spending. Nvidia stock edged 0.3% higher overnight Wednesday. The stock is down 7.3% so far this week and is on track for a seventh straight week in the red. Speaking with Phil Rosen on the Full Signal podcast, Ives, a partner at Yorkville, described Huang as one of U.S.’ most strategically important technology figures, pointing to Nvidia’s central role in the global semiconductor industry and the competition between Washington and Beijing. “Jensen’s the most important technology asset in the United States. Now you could hate him, love him, that’s just factual, that’s the reality. Then it’s like the biggest gating factor  between China and the U.S. is Nvidia and Jensen.” He added that Huang's exit creates a difficult situation for investors. The board must decide whether he can remain CEO as investigations and China-related allegations continue. Ives said the probes could last several months, keeping questions about the company's leadership unresolved. “No doubt, Nvidia is different without Jensen. There’s no way to sugarcoat that.” Despite the leadership questions, Ives remains optimistic about Nvidia’s competitive position. He argued that the company has a technological advantage of roughly two to three years over rival chipmakers. “Without Jensen, let’s just say Jensen sails into the sunset and has his own chip company, goes with Musk to SpaceX, wherever it may be.  We’re still bullish on Nvidia because the reality is they’re two, three years ahead of any competitor, chip-wise.  They’re two, three years ahead of China and they’re the one chip in the world fueling the AI revolution.” Ives said the Nvidia leadership turmoil has made this one of the most unusual weeks of his 27-year career and added that the company’s importance to AI and U.S. business investment makes the situation even more significant. “Nvidia’s the central nervous system, not just of AI, but, I would say of the U.S. economy relative to CapEx.” In its first earnings report since parting ways with Jensen Huang last week, the chip giant posted fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-on-year and above analysts' estimate of $109.3 billion, as per Fiscal.ai. Elon Musk said on Wednesday that Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) would probably be better together, but that closing a merger shouldn’t be enough to earn him the stock awards Tesla tied to its performance. Both stocks rose for a second straight session on Wednesday, with TSLA gaining 1 % and SPCX climbing 1.3%. “You don’t need them to be together, but would they be better together?” Musk said at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit. “Probably yes.” Musk said advances in AI, robotics and chip design had given Tesla and SpaceX a reason to consider a combination that he struggled to see five years ago. Andrew Ross Sorkin, a columnist for The New York Times, raised a question DealBook readers had repeatedly asked about whether a merger should trigger Musk’s Tesla stock awards. “I should not receive those stock option awards simply for merging with SpaceX because that is not meeting the deal, which was that I should only get those stock options for Tesla performance, not just because of a merger,” Musk said. A merger could change how Musk earns his Tesla pay. He called the awards stock options, though Tesla’s filings say his 2025 package consists of 423.7 million shares of performance-based restricted stock. To earn each of the 12 installments, Tesla typically must hit an operating goal and a valuation target, starting at $2 trillion and rising to $8.5 trillion. If the deal’s structure triggered Tesla’s change-in-control clause, shares Musk had already earned would vest. The deal price would factor into Tesla’s valuation, which alone would determine whether he earned more. One way the clause could kick in is if a new owner gained more than half of Tesla’s voting power. An exception applies if Tesla’s existing shareholders keep at least half the voting power in Tesla or its parent company, with their stakes in about the same proportion as before. To work out what Musk earned, Tesla would use whichever is higher: its last closing price or the price shareholders received in the deal. A higher deal could unlock more shares for Musk even if Tesla missed an operating goal. He would give up any part of the award he still had not earned when the deal closed. “If you’d asked me five years ago, do I ever think there’s any purpose in SpaceX and Tesla getting together, I would have said no,” Musk said. Tesla develops AI for self-driving cars and its Optimus robot, while SpaceX builds large AI models and supplies computing power to customers such as Anthropic. Both design advanced chips and already work together on Terafab, their chipmaking venture. Last month, Musk said Terafab was aiming to produce its first test chip in May or June 2027. However, Tesla and SpaceX could pursue the opportunities on their own, Musk said. The case for a merger hinges on whether they could create more value for shareholders together. “These require shareholder votes, which may or may not succeed,” Musk said. He added that his own vote would have to take into account whether the terms made financial sense for other SpaceX investors. Musk confirmed last month that both companies had formed committees of independent directors to explore a deal. An announcement could reportedly come as early as December, but the companies had also discussed early 2027. Before Musk confirmed the merger talks in October, Goldman Sachs had expanded its Tesla options positions while cutting its stake in the automaker by 11.7%. By the end of September, its calls covered 5.66 million Tesla shares, up 186.5% from June. Its puts also nearly doubled to cover 5.24 million shares. MERGER is HERE” Another user said, “$TSLA The SpaceX merger committee will not approve a merger with a company that has a 415P. E! It would be illegal, it would be considered fraud. Either the merger will not happen, or they have to drop. Tesla down to a reasonable number, maybe below 200.” So far this year, TSLA shares are down 15%, while SPCX shares are up 6% from their June IPO price. CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday criticized Nvidia’s board’s decision to oust Jensen Huang as CEO, calling it “like kicking Michael Jordan off of your team when you are on a winning streak .” “I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said about the former Nvidia CEO who was ousted after reports of romantic relations with a Chinese intelligence asset. Musk described Huang as “an old friend of mine” and added that the board’s decision to oust him “doesn't seem like a smart decision to me.” “…there's no one that can really replace Jensen,” Musk said at The New York Times Dealbook Summit. “He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades. He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him, loves him, and many of them are there because of him, and have had higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.” When asked if he sees Huang returning to Nvidia, Musk said that it is ultimately on Nvidia’s board of directors or shareholders. “I think, like the current board would either need to change their mind, or shareholders would need to vote the board out at the shareholders meeting, which is that's that's pretty rare for that to happen. So, but really the board is in charge of the company right now,” the Tesla CEO said. Earlier this week, Nvidia's board chairman firmly stated during the earnings call that Jensen Huang will not be reinstated under any circumstances. Earlier today, it was also reported that a recruitment agency hired by Nvidia’s (NVDA) board has reportedly officially reached out to Arm Holdings (ARM) CEO Rene Haas to take over the reins at the chipmaker. Musk’s companies and Nvidia share deep business ties. SpaceX has publicly committed to building its expanding AI infrastructure, including terrestrial data centers and planned orbital computing, exclusively on Nvidia’s platforms, with Musk describing the Vera Rubin architecture as the best available and stating that the company expects to receive a significant share of Nvidia’s GPU output. Nvidia also holds a stake in SpaceX. Musk’s EV company Tesla, meanwhile, relies on Nvidia hardware for AI training even as it develops its own inference chips for Full Self-Driving and the Optimus robot. Talking about his own comments about wanting to hire Huang at the Summit, Musk asked, “Who wouldn't want to hire Jensen?” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA and SPCX was within the 'bullish' territory at the time of writing. While TSLA stock has slipped 15% year-to-date, SPCX stock is currently trading at about $143.5, above its June IPO price of $135. Nvidia, meanwhile, clocked its fifth consecutive day in the red on Wednesday and is down 19% this year. A sign pointing out the sights and sounds visitors might encounter at College Woods in New Hampshire helped improve their moods, a University of New Hampshire researcher found. “There’s a huge body of evidence saying being in nature is good for us,” said Lauren Ferguson, Ph.D., an assistant professor in the University of New Hampshire’s Department of Recreation Management and Policy. Ferguson conducted research at College Woods in New Hampshire to study how walking outdoors affects people’s feelings. “What I did find is that the perception of biodiversity is more important than the actual biodiversity,” Ferguson said. She found that simply placing a sign at the entrance to College Woods listing the sights and sounds visitors might encounter had a positive effect on their moods. Ferguson said people’s perceptions of their surroundings mattered more than the specific sights they encountered. The sign also made visitors more aware of their surroundings by telling them what to look for, making the experience more restorative. “Our normal day-to-day life is extremely cognitively depleting, but being in a place like this allows your brain to still remain focused and remain engaged while you’re also simultaneously recovering from that fatigue,” Ferguson said. Ferguson said the biggest positive effects were seen during warmer months, but nature walks can improve mood in any season. She encourages people to take walks outdoors, even during colder months.
